message.content: {"summary":"Excellent work across all six questions. Your Q1 scenarios were complete and measurable, Q3 calculations were fully correct with working shown, and your Q2, Q4, Q5 and Q6 answers showed scenario-specific reasoning, correct CAP usage and balanced consequences. The only gap is format: Question 2 appears marginally over the 150-word limit, which held Communication at Proficient. Tighten word counts to reach the top level there.","next_steps":["Trim Question 2 to 150 words or fewer by cutting general background and keeping the recommendation and trade-offs","Check every answer against the word limit before submission, as one overrun cost a mark here","Keep citing sources in IEEE style and using the required headings, which you did well"],"criteria":{"C1":"Excellent. You chose performance and availability and justified them from scenario data (900 orders/hour, 4.2 s p95, payment outage). Both scenarios had all six parts with measurable response measures, e.g. 'p95 response time under 1.5 s and no requests dropped'. This is exactly what the top rubric level requires; maintain this standard.","C2":"Excellent. Your modular monolith recommendation was justified by two scenario-specific trade-offs (team size, lunchtime load from a single VM) and you explicitly acknowledged the downside that modules cannot be scaled independently. To stay at this level, keep trade-offs anchored to the scenario rather than textbook points.","C3":"Excellent. All parts verified correct: series availability 0.99301 (99.30%), downtime 5.0 h; parallel payment 0.999975 giving 99.80% and 1.5 h downtime. Working was shown to the requested precision. Keep showing your working step by step, as this is what full marks depend on.","C4":"Excellent. You named the Circuit Breaker pattern, explained the Closed/Open/Half-Open mechanism correctly, applied it to the payment outage, and gave both a tuning consideration (thresholds from real latency data) and a drawback. This covers every element of the top level; sustain this completeness in future answers.","C5":"Excellent. Both consistency/availability choices were justified, CAP was used correctly (P not optional), and concrete techniques were named for each case (Redis with 60-second TTL; idempotency keys). Your framing of rejecting orders with a clear error rather than risking inconsistent charges was strong applied reasoning.","C6":"Excellent. Context, Decision and Consequences were all present and scenario-specific, with both positive and negative consequences, e.g. the queue being one more component for five developers to run. Balanced consequences are what distinguish Excellent from Proficient; you did this well.","C7":"Proficient. Headings were used in order, IEEE citations and a reference list were present, and terminology was precise. The single issue was Question 2 appearing marginally over the 150-word limit. To reach Excellent, ensure every answer is within 150 words and double-check counts before submitting."}}
